title: Web Push support for gundeck (RFC 8030/8291/8292)
description:
# Web Push support for gundeck (RFC 8030/8291/8292)

## Goal
Extend wire-server's push infrastructure to deliver notifications to **web browsers** via the W3C Push API, alongside the existing native (GCM/APNS) push that runs through AWS SNS.

## Why it's a distinct subsystem
Web push is **architecturally decoupled from AWS SNS** — AWS SNS has no web-push platform. Instead gundeck acts as the RFC 8030 *application server*: it stores browser-supplied subscription endpoints and POSTs to them directly, encrypting the body per RFC 8291 (ECDH P-256 + HKDF + AES-128-GCM) and authenticating per RFC 8292 (VAPID JWT).

```
                ┌──── native (unchanged) ────┐
pushAllLegacy ──┼─► pushNative ─► AWS SNS     │
                │
                └─► pushWeb   ─► HTTPS POST to browser push-service endpoint
                                (RFC 8291 encrypt + RFC 8292 VAPID)
```

## Key design decisions (confirmed)
- **Separate `WebPushSubscription` type + route** (not a new `Transport` variant on `PushToken`), because the subscription shape (endpoint URL + p256dh + auth) is structurally different from a native token, and dispatch cannot use SNS.
- **Static VAPID key from config** (server's P-256 private key in gundeck settings; public key advertised to web clients out-of-band). Simplest, stable identifier.
- **No new external dependencies**: crypto from `crypton` (already transitive via `saml2-web-sso`), JWT from `jose` (already in `wire-api`).

## Relevant specs
- W3C Push API — subscription object `{endpoint, keys:{p256dh,auth}, expirationTime}`
- RFC 8030 — Web Push protocol (POST to endpoint, TTL/Urgency/Topic headers)
- RFC 8291 — Message Encryption (aes128gcm content coding, 86-byte header)
- RFC 8292 — VAPID (application server identification via ES256 JWT)

## Layer map (children)
1. WP-API   — API types + routes (wire-api)
2. WP-DB    — Cassandra migration V13
3. WP-CFG   — Config (WebPushOpts + VAPID keypair in Env)
4. WP-STORE — Storage layer (Gundeck/Push/Web/Data.hs)
5. WP-CRYPTO — RFC 8291/8292 crypto module
6. WP-HANDLERS — API handlers (add/delete/list)
7. WP-DISPATCH — Web dispatch (HTTPS POST)
8. WP-ROUTES — Route wiring (Gundeck/API/Public.hs)
9. WP-FLOW  — Hook into pushAllLegacy
10. WP-TESTS — Golden + roundtrip + crypto KAT
11. WP-QA    — Quality gate (build/format/lint/nix)

## Out of scope (v1)
- Declarative push messages (W3C §3.3) — we send the same opaque notice payload as native.
- Client-side service-worker code.
- Migration tooling for existing native tokens.
close_reason: All 11 children complete (100%). Web push (RFC 8030/8291/8292) fully integrated across wire-api, wire-subsystems, and gundeck. Final QA gate (wire-server-5qh.11) passed with zero drift: make c clean (-Werror), all unit suites green (wire-api 467, wire-subsystems 311, gundeck 123 incl. RFC 8291 crypto KAT), ormolu/hlint clean, nix aligned, no secrets in repo.

# Tests — Golden + roundtrip + crypto KAT + unit

## Objective
Cover correctness of types, crypto (the security-critical part), and dispatch logic.

## Files to create / change
- **NEW** `libs/wire-api/test/golden/Test/Wire/API/Golden/Generated/WebPushSubscription_user.hs` (mirror `PushToken_user.hs`)
- **EDIT** `libs/wire-api/test/golden/Test/Wire/API/Golden/Generated.hs` (register group, lines 156-157, 827-830)

## Crypto KAT (MUST pass) — the core correctness proof
Encrypt `"When I grow up, I want to be a watermelon"` using the RFC 8291 §5 / Appendix A test vectors and assert byte-identical ciphertext:

```
Plaintext:        V2hlbiBJIGdyb3cgdXAsIEkgd2FudCB0byBiZSBhIHdhdGVybWVsb24
ua_public:        BCVxsr7N_eNgVRqvHtD0zTZsEc6-VV-JvLexhqUzORcxaOzi6-AYWXvTBHm4bjyPjs7Vd8pZGH6SRpkNtoIAiw4
ua_private:       q1dXpw3UpT5VOmu_cf_v6ih07Aems3njxI-JWgLcM94
as_public:        BP4z9KsN6nGRTbVYI_c7VJSPQTBtkgcy27mlmlMoZIIgDll6e3vCYLocInmYWAmS6TlzAC8wEqKK6PBru3jl7A8
as_private:       yfWPiYE-n46HLnH0KqZOF1fJJU3MYrct3AELtAQ-oRw

salt:             DGv6ra1nlYgDCS1FRnbzlw
Expected body:    DGv6ra1nlYgDCS1FRnbzlwAAEABBBP4z9KsN6nGRTbVYI... (RFC 8291 §5)
```
Also assert intermediate values (ecdh_secret, IKM, CEK, NONCE) match Appendix A if practical.

## Other unit tests
- `signVapid` JWT decodes with the expected `aud`/`sub`/`exp` and verifies against the public key.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `make c package=wire-api test=1` green (golden + roundtrip).
- [ ] `make c package=gundeck test=1` green (crypto KAT + dispatch unit).
- [ ] Crypto KAT assertion is present and passing — not just "compiles".

- `libs/wire-api/test/golden/Test/Wire/API/Golden/Generated/PushToken_user.hs` (golden pattern)

title: WP-QA: Quality gate (build/format/lint/nix align)
description:
# Quality gate — build, format, lint, align Nix

## Objective
Satisfy the project's quality expectations (AGENTS.md) before declaring web push done. Run after all other WP-* beads are closed.

## Checklist
1. **Type check, whole project, no warnings:**
   `make c | grep -vE 'Compiling|Linking|Preprocessing|Configuring|Building'`
2. **Unit tests green (all changed packages):**
   `make c test=1 | grep -vE 'Compiling|Linking|Preprocessing|Configuring|Building'`
   (at minimum `wire-api` and `gundeck`; run others touched)
3. **Format:**
   `make format` (ormolu --mode inplace on all changed .hs files)
4. **Lint:**
   `make lint-all` (hlint)
5. **Align Cabal/Nix deps:**
   `make regen-local-nix-derivations` — especially relevant if `crypton`/`jose` were added explicitly to `gundeck.cabal` build-depends in WP-CRYPTO.
6. **Review diff:**
   `git diff` — confirm no stray debug logs, no committed secrets (the VAPID private key MUST come from config/env, never the repo).
7. **Do NOT run integration tests** (`make ci` or `*-integration` suites) per AGENTS.md — they depend on specific environments.

## Pre-commit validation
- No compiler warnings introduced.
- `crypton`/`jose` deps resolved correctly in nix after regen.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `make c` clean across whole repo.
- [ ] `make c test=1` green for changed packages.
- [ ] `make format` produces no further diff.
- [ ] `make lint-all` clean.
- [ ] `make regen-local-nix-derivations` shows no Cabal/Nix drift.
- [ ] `git diff` reviewed; no secrets in repo.

## References
- `AGENTS.md` (Quality expectations; Agent commandments)
- Depends on: ALL other WP-* beads

title: WP-CFG: WebPushOpts + VAPID keypair in gundeck Env
description:
# Layer 6 — Config: WebPushOpts + VAPID keypair

## Objective
Make the server's VAPID P-256 key pair and web-push settings configurable, and load the keypair into `Env` at startup.

## Files to change
- **EDIT** `services/gundeck/src/Gundeck/Options.hs` — add `WebPushOpts`
- **EDIT** `services/gundeck/src/Gundeck/Env.hs` — parse keypair, store in `Env`
- **EDIT** deployment config sample (if present, e.g. `services/gundeck/` yaml under `deploy/`)

## WebPushOpts (Options.hs)
```haskell
data WebPushOpts = WebPushOpts
  { _vapidSubject      :: !Text        -- e.g. "mailto:ops@wire.com" or "https://wire.com"
  , _vapidPrivateKey   :: !Text        -- P-256 private key, base64url (raw 32 bytes) or PEM
  , _endpointAllowlist :: ![Text]      -- allowed push-service host suffixes (SSRF mitigation)
  , _defaultTTL        :: !(Maybe Word32)
  }
  deriving (Show, Generic)

deriveFromJSON toOptionFieldName ''WebPushOpts
makeLenses ''WebPushOpts
```
Add `_webpush :: !WebPushOpts` to `Opts` (around line 133).

## Env (Env.hs)
- Define `data VapidKeyPair = VapidKeyPair { vkpPrivate :: PrivateKey, vkpPublic :: PublicKey }` (crypton P-256 types) plus the derived base64url public key string for the client-facing endpoint.
- In `createEnv` (line 69), decode `_vapidPrivateKey`, validate it is a valid P-256 scalar in range, derive the public point, and store a `VapidKeyPair` in `Env`.
- Add `_vapid :: !VapidKeyPair` to `Env` (line 53).

## Public key endpoint (hand-off to WP-ROUTES)
Expose `GET /push/web/vapid-public-key` returning the uncompressed/base64url public key so web clients can pass it as `applicationServerKey` to `pushManager.subscribe()`. (Route wiring done in WP-ROUTES; key retrieval done here.)

## Security
- The private key is a long-lived secret: must come from a secret manager / env, never committed. Document loading via env var override (same pattern as `REDIS_PASSWORD` at `Env.hs:80`).
- Validate `vapidSubject` is a `mailto:` or `https://` URL (RFC 8292 §3).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Missing/malformed VAPID key fails fast at startup with a clear error.
- [ ] `Env` carries the parsed `VapidKeyPair`.
- [ ] Public key endpoint returns the base64url uncompressed point.

## References
- `services/gundeck/src/Gundeck/Options.hs:133-155` (Opts pattern)
- `services/gundeck/src/Gundeck/Env.hs:69-108` (createEnv)
- RFC 8292 §2-3 (VAPID key format, JWT claims)
close_reason:
Implemented WP-CFG: WebPushOpts (Maybe, optional section) + VapidKeyPair in Env. Pure parse/validate helpers (mkVapidKeyPair/parseVapidKeyPair/validateVapidSubject) with explicit scalarIsValid range check (rejects d=0 and d>=n, since crypton's decodePrivate only checks byte length). Env override GUNDECK_WEBPUSH_VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY mirrors REDIS_PASSWORD. Redacting Show instance on WebPushOpts (repo convention). RFC 8291 Appendix A KAT verifies the full crypto chain. 34/34 unit tests green, build clean, hlint clean, nix aligned. Commit cbace5a1e.

Design deviation (documented in commit): _webpush :: Maybe WebPushOpts / _vapid :: Maybe VapidKeyPair instead of non-Maybe, so absent config disables web push (incremental rollout, no breakage to existing deployments) and present-but-invalid fails fast. Downstream beads WP-CRYPTO/WP-ROUTES/WP-DISPATCH consume Env._vapid :: Maybe VapidKeyPair and must handle Nothing (feature disabled).

title: WP-CRYPTO: RFC 8291 encryption + RFC 8292 VAPID signing
description:
# Layer 3 — Crypto: RFC 8291 encryption + RFC 8292 VAPID signing

## Objective
Implement the two crypto primitives web push requires, using `crypton`. This is the correctness-critical core.

## Files to create / change
- **NEW** `services/gundeck/src/Gundeck/Push/Web/Crypto.hs`
- **EDIT** `services/gundeck/gundeck.cabal` — add `crypton` (and possibly `jose`) to build-depends if not already visible transitively.

## Public API
```haskell
-- RFC 8291: produce the aes128gcm content-coded body.
-- 86-byte header (salt(16) || rs=4096(4) || idlen=65(1) || as_public(65)) + single encrypted record.
encryptPayload ::
     WebPushKeys        -- recipient p256dh (ECDH pub) + auth secret
  -> ByteString         -- plaintext (MUST be <= 3993 bytes per RFC 8291 §4)
  -> IO EncryptedBody   -- generates ephemeral ECDH keypair + 16-byte salt internally

-- RFC 8292: VAPID JWT (ES256) + header values.
signVapid ::
     VapidKeyPair       -- server's static P-256 key (from WP-CFG)
  -> Text               -- subject (mailto: or https://)
  -> Text               -- audience origin, e.g. "https://fcm.googleapis.com"
  -> IO VapidHeaders    -- { authorization :: "vapid t=<jwt>,k=<kid>", cryptoKey :: "p256ecdsa=<pub>" }
```

## Implementation — follow RFC 8291 §3.4 pseudocode verbatim
1. **ECDH P-256**: generate ephemeral keypair; `ecdh_secret = ECDH(as_private, ua_public)`. Use `Crypto.PubKey.ECC.DH` (crypton).
2. **Validate** the recipient `p256dh` point is on the P-256 curve (RFC 8291 §7) — prevents invalid-curve attacks. Steps: not point-at-infinity; coords in range; satisfies curve equation.
3. **HKDF-SHA256 key combine** (`Crypto.KDF.HKDF`):
   - `salt = auth_secret`, `IKM = ecdh_secret`
   - `key_info = "WebPush: info" || 0x00 || ua_public || as_public`
   - `IKM' = HMAC-SHA256(salt=auth_secret, key_info || 0x01)` → 32 bytes
4. **RFC 8188 CEK/nonce** (HKDF with `salt = random 16-byte salt`):
   - `PRK = HMAC-SHA256(salt, IKM')`
   - `CEK   = HMAC-SHA256(PRK, "Content-Encoding: aes128gcm" || 0x00 || 0x01)[0..15]`
   - `NONCE = HMAC-SHA256(PRK, "Content-Encoding: nonce"      || 0x00 || 0x01)[0..11]`
5. **AES-128-GCM** (`Crypto.Cipher.AES` + `Crypto.Cipher.Types.aeadEncrypt`): plaintext || padding-delimiter `0x02`, single record, `rs=4096`.
6. **Header**: `salt || rs(4, big-endian) || idlen(1, =65) || as_public(65)` → 86 bytes; concat with ciphertext.

## VAPID JWT (RFC 8292)
- Claims: `{ "aud": <endpoint origin>, "exp": <now+12h>, "sub": <subject> }`.
- Signed ES256 (ECDSA P-256 SHA-256) with the server private key. Use `jose` (already a wire-api dep) or raw `Crypto.PubKey.ECDSA.sign`.
- Header dict: `Authorization: vapid t=<jwt>,k=<kid>`; `Crypto-Key: p256ecdsa=<base64url pub>`.

## Acceptance criteria — MUST pass the RFC 8291 known-answer test
- [ ] Encrypt the plaintext `"When I grow up, I want to be a watermelon"` with the RFC 8291 §5 / Appendix A test vectors (keys, salt, auth secret provided) and reproduce the exact ciphertext from §5. **This is the primary correctness proof.**
- [ ] `signVapid` produces a JWT verifiable against the derived public key.
- [ ] Rejects a `p256dh` not on the curve.

## References
- RFC 8291 §3.4 (pseudocode), §4 (record restrictions), §5 + Appendix A (test vectors)
- RFC 8292 §2-3
- Depends on: WP-CFG (VapidKeyPair), WP-API (WebPushKeys)

title: WP-API: API types + routes for WebPushSubscription (wire-api)
description:
# Layer 1 — API types + routes (libs/wire-api)

## Objective
Define the public API contract for web push subscriptions in `wire-api`, consumed by gundeck and by clients.

## Files to create / change
- **NEW** `libs/wire-api/src/Wire/API/Push/V2/WebSubscription.hs` — types
- **EDIT** `libs/wire-api/src/Wire/API/Routes/Public/Gundeck.hs` — add `WebPushAPI` to `GundeckAPI` (currently line 34)
- **EDIT** `libs/wire-api/src/Wire/API/Push/V2.hs` — re-export new types (around line 58)
- **NEW** `libs/wire-api/test/golden/Test/Wire/API/Golden/Generated/WebPushSubscription_user.hs`
- **EDIT** `libs/wire-api/test/golden/Test/Wire/API/Golden/Generated.hs` — register golden group (mirror `PushToken_user` at lines 156-157, 827-830)
- **EDIT** `libs/wire-api/test/unit/Test/Wire/API/Roundtrip/Aeson.hs` — add roundtrip (near line 212)

## Types to define (in WebSubscription.hs)
```haskell
newtype EndpointUrl = EndpointUrl { endpointUrlText :: Text }
  -- MUST validate: parses as https:// URI (RFC 8030 §8.2: must not leak user identity)

newtype P256dhKey  = P256dhKey  { ... }  -- base64url, 65 bytes uncompressed P-256 point
newtype AuthSecret = AuthSecret { ... }  -- base64url, 16 bytes

data WebPushKeys = WebPushKeys
  { _wpkP256dh :: !P256dhKey
  , _wpkAuth   :: !AuthSecret
  }

data WebPushSubscription = WebPushSubscription
  { _wpsEndpoint       :: !EndpointUrl
  , _wpsKeys           :: !WebPushKeys
  , _wpsExpirationTime :: !(Maybe Word64)   -- ms since epoch; Nothing = no expiry
  , _wpsClient         :: !ClientId
  }

newtype WebPushSubscriptionList = WebPushSubscriptionList { wpsList :: [WebPushSubscription] }
```
- Derive `ToSchema`/`FromJSON`/`Arbitrary` via `Schema` (same pattern as `PushToken` in `Token.hs:79-109`).
- Define API response types mirroring `AddTokenError`/`AddTokenSuccess`/`AddTokenResponses` in `Token.hs:191-219`: `AddWebPushError`, `AddWebPushSuccess`, `AddWebPushResponses`, `DeleteWebPushResponses`.

## Routes (in Gundeck.hs)
```haskell
type GundeckAPI = PushAPI :<|> WebPushAPI :<|> NotificationAPI :<|> TimeAPI

type WebPushAPI =
  Named "register-web-push-subscription"
    ( Summary "Register a web push subscription"
        :> From '<>> '<latest-version>      -- gate behind new API version (see how get-server-time uses From 'V9, line 139)
        :> ZUser
        :> "push" :> "web" :> "subscriptions"
        :> ReqBody '[JSON] WebPushSubscription
        :> MultiVerb 'POST '[JSON] AddWebPushResponses (Either AddWebPushError AddWebPushSuccess) )
  :<|> Named "delete-web-push-subscription"
        ( ... :> Capture "endpoint" EndpointUrl :> MultiVerb 'DELETE '[JSON] DeleteWebPushResponses (Maybe ()) )
  :<|> Named "get-web-push-subscriptions"
        ( ... :> Get '[JSON] WebPushSubscriptionList )
```

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `make c package=wire-api` compiles with no warnings.
- [ ] Golden JSON roundtrips for `WebPushSubscription`.
- [ ] `EndpointUrl` rejects non-https inputs.
- [ ] OpenAPI schema renders the new routes.

## References
- `libs/wire-api/src/Wire/API/Push/V2/Token.hs:79-219` (pattern to mirror)
- `libs/wire-api/src/Wire/API/Routes/Public/Gundeck.hs:34-65` (route pattern)
- W3C Push API §3.4 (PushSubscription), §8 (interface)
close_reason:
Implemented all API types and routes for WebPushSubscription.

Created Wire.API.Push.V2.WebSubscription with:
- EndpointUrl (HTTPS-only), P256dhKey (65 bytes), AuthSecret (16 bytes)
- WebPushKeys, WebPushSubscription, WebPushSubscriptionList
- AddWebPushError/Success response types, DeleteWebPushRequest
- Three routes (POST/DELETE/GET /push/web/subscriptions), all From 'V17
- DELETE uses ReqBody with DeleteWebPushRequest (not Capture) to avoid URL-encoding issues with endpoint URLs containing slashes
- Gundeck stub handlers for compilation
- Golden + roundtrip tests for all new types

All tests pass: 462 unit + 2980 golden. Whole project type-checks with no warnings.

title: WP-DB: WebPushStore effect + Postgres interpreter + migration (wire-subsystems)
description:
# Layer 2 — WebPushStore effect + Postgres interpreter + migration (libs/wire-subsystems)

## Objective
Define web-push subscription persistence as a **Polysemy effect** with a **Postgres interpreter**, mirroring the `Wire.CodeStore` + `Wire.CodeStore.Postgres` pattern. This is a *library* concern (in `wire-subsystems`), NOT a gundeck-owned Cassandra table. Gundeck-side wiring (pool + Sem runner) is in WP-STORE.

## Why not Cassandra
Per design decision: web push storage moves off Cassandra onto Postgres, structured as a reusable effect. This keeps web push decoupled from gundeck's legacy Cassandra stack and consistent with the refactored services (galley/brig) that already consume `wire-subsystems` effects.

## Files to create / change
- **NEW** `libs/wire-subsystems/postgres-migrations/<YYYYMMDDhhmmss>-create-webpush-subscriptions.sql`
- **NEW** `libs/wire-subsystems/src/Wire/WebPushStore.hs` — effect (mirror `Wire.CodeStore.hs`)
- **NEW** `libs/wire-subsystems/src/Wire/WebPushStore/Postgres.hs` — interpreter (mirror `Wire.CodeStore.Postgres.hs`)
- **EDIT** `libs/wire-subsystems/wire-subsystems.cabal` — expose new modules
- **EDIT** `libs/wire-api/...` (or wire-subsystems) — add `PostgresMarshall` instances for `EndpointUrl`, `P256dhKey`, `AuthSecret` (needed by `lmapPG`/`dimapPG`; see `Wire.API.PostgresMarshall`)

## Migration SQL (timestamped file, auto-picked-up by `Wire.PostgresMigrations` `embedDir`)
```sql
CREATE TABLE webpush_subscriptions (
    user_id    uuid     NOT NULL,
    client_id  uuid     NOT NULL,
    endpoint   text     NOT NULL,    -- browser push-service URL
    p256dh     text     NOT NULL,    -- base64url ECDH P-256 pub key (65B uncompressed)
    auth       text     NOT NULL,    -- base64url auth secret (16B)
    expiration bigint,               -- ms since epoch; NULL = no expiry
    conn_id    text     NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (user_id, client_id, endpoint)
);
-- leading PK column user_id already indexes the per-user lookup hot path.
```
NOTE: migrations are SQL files dropped into the `postgres-migrations/` dir and sorted by filename timestamp — NOT a Haskell V13 module. No edit to `Gundeck.Schema.Run`.

## Effect (Wire/WebPushStore.hs) — like CodeStore
```haskell
module Wire.WebPushStore where
import Data.Id (ClientId, ConnId, UserId)
import Imports
import Polysemy
import Wire.API.Push.V2.WebSubscription  -- from WP-API

data WebPushStore m a where
  InsertSubscription  :: UserId -> WebPushSubscription -> ConnId -> WebPushStore m ()
  LookupSubscriptions :: UserId -> WebPushStore m [WebPushAddress]
  DeleteSubscription  :: UserId -> EndpointUrl -> WebPushStore m ()
  DeleteAllForUser    :: UserId -> WebPushStore m ()    -- GDPR / account delete
  PurgeExpired        :: UserId -> WebPushStore m ()

makeSem ''WebPushStore
```
`WebPushAddress` is the dispatch-time record (user, conn, endpoint, keys, client) — analogous to `Address` in `Native/Types.hs:52`. Define it here or in a sibling `Wire/WebPushStore/Types.hs`.

## Interpreter (Wire/WebPushStore/Postgres.hs) — like CodeStore.Postgres
```haskell
module Wire.WebPushStore.Postgres (interpretWebPushStoreToPostgres) where
import Wire.Postgres
import Wire.API.PostgresMarshall
import Hasql.TH
...

interpretWebPushStoreToPostgres :: (PGConstraints r) => InterpreterFor WebPushStore r
interpretWebPushStoreToPostgres = interpret $ \case
  InsertSubscription uid sub conn -> insertSubscriptionImpl uid sub conn
  LookupSubscriptions uid         -> lookupSubscriptionsImpl uid
  DeleteSubscription uid ep       -> runStatement (uid, ep) deleteSub
  DeleteAllForUser uid            -> runStatement uid deleteAll
  PurgeExpired uid                -> purgeExpiredImpl uid
```
Queries via Hasql TH quasi-quoters:
- `insertSub`: `[resultlessStatement| INSERT INTO webpush_subscriptions (...) VALUES (...) ON CONFLICT (user_id, client_id, endpoint) DO UPDATE SET ... |]` (upsert — re-register updates keys/expiry, no duplicate).
- `lookupSubscriptionsImpl`: multi-row select `WHERE user_id = ($1 :: uuid)` using the vector/list Hasql.TH quasi-quoter; decode each row to `WebPushAddress`.
- `deleteSub` / `deleteAll`: `resultlessStatement` DELETEs.
- `purgeExpiredImpl`: `DELETE ... WHERE user_id = $1 AND expiration IS NOT NULL AND expiration < <now_ms>`.

Use `lmapPG`/`dimapPG` (from `Wire.API.PostgresMarshall`) to encode/decode domain types exactly like `CodeStore.Postgres.hs:65-100`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `make c package=wire-subsystems` compiles (effect + interpreter).
- [ ] Migration file present and sorted; `Wire.PostgresMigrations.allMigrations` picks it up.
- [ ] `InsertSubscription` then `LookupSubscriptions` round-trips; re-insert upserts.
- [ ] `PurgeExpired` removes only expired rows.

## References
- `libs/wire-subsystems/src/Wire/CodeStore.hs` (effect template)
- `libs/wire-subsystems/src/Wire/CodeStore/Postgres.hs` (interpreter template)
- `libs/wire-subsystems/src/Wire/Postgres.hs:94-155` (`PGConstraints`, `runStatement`)
- `libs/wire-subsystems/src/Wire/PostgresMigrations.hs:40-41` (`embedDir` migration pickup)
- `libs/wire-subsystems/src/Wire/AppStore/Postgres.hs` (second interpreter example)
- Depends on: WP-API (types: `WebPushSubscription`, `EndpointUrl`, `WebPushKeys`)
close_reason:
Implemented WebPushStore effect + Postgres interpreter + migration.

Created Wire.WebPushStore (effect + WebPushAddress dispatch record with 5 ops:
insert/lookup/delete/deleteAll/purgeExpired) and Wire.WebPushStore.Postgres
(Hasql.TH interpreter with upsert ON CONFLICT, multi-row vectorStatement lookup,
expiry-based purge). Migration 20260617140000-create-webpush-subscriptions.sql
(PK user_id, client_id, endpoint) auto-picked-up by embedDir.

Added PostgresMarshall instances in wire-api for EndpointUrl (text, HTTPS-validated),
P256dhKey/AuthSecret (text, base64url), ConnId (bytea - matches Cassandra CqlBlob
convention), Word64 (int8). Custom Show on WebPushAddress redacts wpaKeys to avoid
leaking the RFC 8291 auth secret (mirrors native Address pattern, per code review).

In-memory mock interpreter for downstream tests. Roundtrip property tests for all
new marshall pairs.

All tests pass: 467 (wire-api) + 311 (wire-subsystems). Whole project type-checks.
ormolu + hlint clean.

title: WP-FLOW: Hook web push into pushAllLegacy dispatch flow
description:
# Layer (integration) — Hook web push into the pushAllLegacy flow

## Objective
Make web push recipients actually receive notifications: alongside native push dispatch, look up web subscriptions and dispatch via WP-DISPATCH.

## Files to change
- **EDIT** `services/gundeck/src/Gundeck/Push.hs` — extend `pushAllLegacy` (line 271) and the `MonadPushAll` class (line 106)

## Approach
1. Add to `MonadPushAll` (line 106):
   ```haskell
   mpaPushWeb :: Notification -> Priority -> [WebPushAddress] -> m ()
   mpaWebTargets :: UserId -> m [WebPushAddress]   -- or reuse a generic targets effect
   ```
   Instance in `Gundeck` (line 120) calls `Web.push` / `Web.Data.lookup`.

2. In `pushAllLegacy` (line 271), after the existing `pushNativeWithBudget` (line 292), add an analogous `pushWebWithBudget` that:
   - collects web recipients (same `dontPush` set semantics as `nativeTargets`, line 491),
   - looks up `WebPushAddress` per recipient,
   - calls `Web.push`.

3. Respect the same `perNativePushConcurrency` budget (or a new `perWebPushConcurrency`) so web push doesn't overwhelm the manager / external push services. Web push is unmediated (no SNS throttling), so budgeting matters more here.

## Filtering
- Apply the same `shouldActuallyPush` / `eligibleClient` / `whitelistedOrNoWhitelist` logic as `nativeTargets` (lines 452-519) so origin-exclusion and connection allowlists behave identically for web and native.
- Transient pushes (`pushTransient`) skip native (line 304); decide whether web push should also be skipped for transient (recommend: skip, matching native semantics — web push is for durable notices).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A user with only a web subscription receives the notice (encrypted POST fired).
- [ ] A user with both native + web receives both, unless already served over websocket (`dontPush`).
- [ ] Budget limits web-push concurrency.
- [ ] Origin client excluded.

## References
- `services/gundeck/src/Gundeck/Push.hs:271-306` (pushAllLegacy / pushNativeWithBudget)
- `services/gundeck/src/Gundeck/Push.hs:474-523` (pushNative / nativeTargets)
- Depends on: WP-DISPATCH (Web.push), WP-ROUTES (so routes exist), WP-STORE (lookup)
close_reason:
WP-FLOW complete: web push hooked into pushAllLegacy alongside native push.

PRODUCTION (services/gundeck/src/Gundeck/Push.hs):
- MonadPushAll class extended with mpaPushWeb (wraps WebPush.push) and mpaWebTargets (Postgres lookup via runWebPush, log+[] on failure for resilient default).
- pushWebWithBudget: mirror of pushNativeWithBudget (same transient skip, same mpaRunWithBudget cost).
- webTargets: mirror of nativeTargets with the same 4 filters (origin/eligibleClient/whitelist/dontPush) adapted for WebPushAddress fields.
- pushAllLegacy: calls pushWebWithBudget after pushNativeWithBudget with the SAME dontPush set.

TESTS:
- MockGundeck: MockEnv refactored to record with _meWebSubscriptions fixture; MockState gained _msWebPushQueue; Arbitrary/ToJSON/FromJSON WebPushAddress orphans; genMockEnv generates 0..2 web subs per (user, client); handlePushWeb mirrors handlePushNative + two extra conditions (not-ws-served matching production dontPush, and not-consumable because web push is only dispatched from pushAllLegacy never pushAllViaRabbitMq).
- Push.hs: 5 explicit regression tests (web-only, both-subscribed offline, ws-served skip, origin skip, transient skip) plus the existing property test (pushAllProp) automatically extends via whole-state equality.

VERIFICATION (2026-06-18):
- make c (whole project) clean, no warnings.
- make c package=gundeck test=1 -> All 123 tests passed (was 118; +5 new explicit web push flow cases).
- ormolu + hlint clean.
- Code-reviewed by code-reviewer agent: APPROVE with one MEDIUM finding (singleUserEnv consumability hardening) addressed before commit.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
[x] A user with only a web subscription receives the notice (web-only test).
[x] A user with both native + web receives both, unless already served over websocket (both-subscribed offline test + ws-served-skip test).
[x] Budget limits web-push concurrency (pushWebWithBudget uses mpaRunWithBudget like native; WebPush.push uses perNativePushConcurrency).
[x] Origin client excluded (origin-client-skip test).

DESIGN DECISIONS:
- Web push dispatched ONLY from pushAllLegacy (not pushAllViaRabbitMq). Consumable (rabbitmq-routed) clients do not get web push because they receive notifications via the persistent rabbitmq queue. This asymmetry vs. native push (which is dispatched from both pipelines) is documented in handlePushWeb and tested via the notConsumable filter.
- Reused perNativePushConcurrency budget (per spec) instead of adding a separate perWebPushConcurrency.
- mpaWebTargets returns [] on PG failure (resilient default) rather than throwing, to isolate per-user lookup failures from the entire push batch.

title: WP-HANDLERS: register/delete/list web push handlers
description:
# Layer 5.1 — API handlers (Gundeck/Push.hs)

## Objective
Implement the request handlers for register/delete/list web push subscriptions, mirroring `addToken`/`deleteToken`/`listTokens`.

## Files to change
- **EDIT** `services/gundeck/src/Gundeck/Push.hs` — add `addWebSubscription`, `deleteWebSubscription`, `listWebSubscriptions` (near the native handlers at lines 527-689)

## Handlers
```haskell
addWebSubscription :: UserId -> WebPushSubscription -> Gundeck (Either AddWebPushError AddWebPushSuccess)
addWebSubscription uid sub = ...
  -- validate: EndpointUrl is https AND host matches endpointAllowlist (SSRF mitigation)
  -- Web.Data.purgeExpired uid
  -- Web.Data.insert uid sub <conn-from-ZConn>
  -- return AddWebPushSuccess sub

deleteWebSubscription :: UserId -> EndpointUrl -> Gundeck (Maybe ())
deleteWebSubscription uid ep = ... Web.Data.delete uid ep $> Just () ...

listWebSubscriptions :: UserId -> Gundeck WebPushSubscriptionList
listWebSubscriptions uid = WebPushSubscriptionList . map (...) <$> Web.Data.lookup uid Data.LocalQuorum
```

## Validation (security — SSRF)
- The `endpoint` URL is attacker-controllable and gundeck will later POST to it. **Reject** any `endpoint` that:
  - is not `https://`, or
  - whose host is not on the configured `_endpointAllowlist` (WP-CFG), or
  - resolves to/contains a private/loopback address (belt-and-suspenders; also enforce a hardened Manager in WP-DISPATCH).
- On invalid endpoint return the `AddWebPushError` equivalent of `AddTokenErrorInvalid`.

## ConnId
- Native `addToken` takes `ConnId` from the `ZConn` route combinator (Gundeck.hs:41). Web subscription route should include `ZConn` too and pass it to `insert`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Registering the same `(client, endpoint)` twice upserts (no duplicate rows).
- [ ] Invalid/non-https/disallowed-host endpoint returns the invalid error.
- [ ] Delete by endpoint removes exactly that row.

## References
- `services/gundeck/src/Gundeck/Push.hs:527-689` (native handlers)
- Depends on: WP-API (types/routes), WP-STORE (storage)
close_reason: Implemented WP-HANDLERS: addWebSubscription/deleteWebSubscription/listWebSubscriptions in Gundeck.Push, wired into servant sitemap (replacing WP-API stubs). Pure SSRF validator (validateEndpointHost/endpointHost) parses hostname via URI.ByteString, dot-boundary host matching, case-insensitive (RFC 3986), rejecting userinfo/prefix/suffix bypasses. addWebSubscription enforces per-user cap (32) before insert (bounds dispatch fan-out + purge cost). All handlers 503 when web push disabled (Nothing); delete idempotent (204); list reports expiration=Nothing (v1 limitation). Added ZConn to register route (wire-api) -- WP-API had shipped without it; needed for WP-FLOW conn filtering. 13 new unit tests (SSRF matrix + roundtrip); all 59 gundeck tests green; build/ormolu/hlint clean; default.nix regenerated. Commit 666dddad9. Design deviations vs task spec: ZConn added to route; TooMany wired up via cap (was assumed dead); delete idempotent-204 (not 404).

title: WP-DISPATCH: Web push HTTPS POST dispatch (RFC 8030)
description:
# Layer 4 — Web dispatch: HTTPS POST to push-service endpoints

## Objective
The runtime counterpart to native `Aws.publish`: encrypt a notice payload (RFC 8291), sign VAPID (RFC 8292), and POST to the browser's push-service endpoint (RFC 8030).

## Files to create / change
- **NEW** `services/gundeck/src/Gundeck/Push/Web.hs` — dispatch loop (mirror `Gundeck/Push/Native.hs`)
- **NEW** `services/gundeck/src/Gundeck/Push/Web/Serialise.hs` — build the plaintext notice JSON (mirror `Native/Serialise.hs`)

## Dispatch (Web.hs) — analogous to Native.push/push1/publish
```haskell
push :: NativePush -> [WebPushAddress] -> Gundeck ()
push m addrs = ... respect perPushConcurrency budget (pooledMapConcurrentlyN) ...

push1 :: NativePush -> WebPushAddress -> Gundeck ()
push1 m a = do
  let plaintext = serialiseWeb m (a ^. wpaUser)         -- JSON: {type:"notice", data:{id}, user}
  vapid  <- signVapid <$> view vapid <*> pure subject <*> pure (origin (a^.wpaEndpoint))
  body   <- liftIO (encryptPayload (a ^. wpaKeys) plaintext)
  resp   <- httpPost (a ^. wpaEndpoint) body vapid (ttl, urgencyFrom (npPriority m))
  case resp of
    201 / 202           -> onSuccess            -- accepted
    404 / 410           -> onGone               -- subscription expired/unsubscribed -> Web.Data.delete + onTokenRemoved
    413                 -> onTooLarge
    429 / 5xx           -> backoff/retry
```

## httpPost
- Use the existing `_manager :: Manager` from `Env` (`Env.hs:57`). **Recommend a separate hardened Manager** with a custom `managerProxy`/`checkResponse` and an egress filter rejecting private IPs (SSRF), configured in `createEnv`. See how `Push/Websocket.hs:200` sets `checkResponse`.
- Headers (RFC 8030):
  - `Content-Encoding: aes128gcm`
  - `TTL: <seconds>` (from `_defaultTTL` or push priority; transient → 0)
  - `Urgency: very-low|low|normal|high` (map from `Priority`; see RFC 8030 §5.3 Table 1)
  - `Topic: <collapse-key>` (optional; RFC 8030 §5.4 for coalescing)
  - `Authorization` / `Crypto-Key` from `signVapid`
- Body = the RFC 8291 encrypted body.

## Serialise (Serialise.hs)
- Same JSON shape as `Native.Serialise.serialise` (`{type:"notice", data:{id}, user}`) — **plaintext**, because encryption happens here, not via SNS. Enforce the RFC 8291 §4 plaintext limit (≤ 3993 bytes).

## Prometheus counters
Mirror `Native.hs:84-122`: `web_push_success`, `web_push_gone`, `web_push_too_large`, `web_push_errors`.

## onTokenRemoved
On 404/410, after deleting the row, emit a `PushRemove`-style event equivalent so the client knows (see `Native.hs:215-221` pattern). Web clients get this via the notification stream, not a native push.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A 201 from the endpoint records success; a 410 deletes the subscription.
- [ ] Retries 429/5xx with backoff, bounded.
- [ ] No unencrypted plaintext reaches the wire.
- [ ] Concurrency bounded by the push budget (does not flood FCM/Mozilla).

## References
- `services/gundeck/src/Gundeck/Push/Native.hs:124-237` (push/push1/publish pattern)
- `services/gundeck/src/Gundeck/Push/Native/Serialise.hs` (serialise pattern)
- `services/gundeck/src/Gundeck/Push/Websocket.hs:192-205` (Manager/checkResponse usage)
- RFC 8030 §5 (request), §5.2 (TTL), §5.3 (Urgency)
- Depends on: WP-STORE (WebPushAddress), WP-CRYPTO (encrypt/sign), WP-CFG (vapid key + manager)
close_reason: Implemented: Gundeck.Push.Web dispatch (push/push1/httpPost + Prometheus counters + bounded retry), Serialise (plaintext JSON + RFC 8291 size guard), Ssrf (private-IP egress filter), hardened _webPushManager in Env. 118 unit tests pass. Code-reviewed and all M1-M4 findings addressed.

title: WP-STORE: Bootstrap Hasql pool + minimal Sem runner in gundeck
description:
# Layer (gundeck-side) — Bootstrap Hasql pool + minimal Sem runner in gundeck

## Objective
Gundeck currently has ZERO Postgres/Polysemy footprint (`grep -ciE "polysemy|hasql|wire-subsystems" gundeck.cabal` = 0; its `Gundeck` monad is `ReaderT Env IO` with Cassandra `MonadClient`). This bead adds the minimal infrastructure to consume the `WebPushStore` effect from WP-DB: a Hasql connection pool, Postgres options, migration execution at startup, and a thin `Sem` runner embedded in the `Gundeck` monad.

## Decision (confirmed)
"Effect in lib, minimal Sem runner in gundeck" — do NOT rewrite gundeck into a full Polysemy app. Only embed the minimal `Sem` interpreter stack needed for `WebPushStore`.

## Files to change
- **EDIT** `services/gundeck/gundeck.cabal` — add deps: `wire-subsystems`, `hasql`, `hasql-pool`, `hasql-th`, `polysemy`, `postgresql-libpq` (as transitive), `postgresql-error-codes` (as needed)
- **EDIT** `services/gundeck/src/Gundeck/Options.hs` — add `PostgresOpts` + `_postgres :: !PostgresOpts` to `Opts`
- **EDIT** `services/gundeck/src/Gundeck/Env.hs` — acquire `Hasql.Pool` in `createEnv`, store in `Env`; run migrations at startup
- **EDIT** `services/gundeck/src/Gundeck/Run.hs` (or `Env.hs`) — call `Wire.PostgresMigrations.runAllMigrations` before serving
- **NEW** `services/gundeck/src/Gundeck/Push/Web/Runner.hs` — the minimal `Sem` runner (below)

## PostgresOpts (Options.hs)
```haskell
data PostgresOpts = PostgresOpts
  { _host     :: !Text
  , _port     :: !Word16
  , _db       :: !Text
  , _user     :: !Text
  , _password :: !(Maybe Text)   -- from env to avoid committing secrets (pattern: REDIS_PASSWORD, Env.hs:80)
  , _poolSize :: !(Maybe Int)
  }
  deriving (Show, Generic)
deriveFromJSON toOptionFieldName ''PostgresOpts
makeLenses ''PostgresOpts
```
Add `_postgres :: !PostgresOpts` to `Opts` (Gundeck/Options.hs:133). Build the Hasql connection string from these.

## Pool + migrations (Env.hs, createEnv ~line 69)
```haskell
import Hasql.Pool qualified as Hasql
import Wire.PostgresMigrations qualified as PgMigrations

-- in createEnv:
pgPool <- Hasql.acquire (poolSize, connSettings)   -- connSettings from PostgresOpts
PgMigrations.runAllMigrations pgPool l             -- runs webpush migration from wire-subsystems
-- store pgPool in Env as _pgPool :: !Hasql.Pool
```

## Minimal Sem runner (Gundeck/Push/Web/Runner.hs)
```haskell
module Gundeck.Push.Web.Runner (runWebPush) where
import Hasql.Pool (Pool)
import Hasql.Errors (UsageError)
import Polysemy
import Polysemy.Error (runError)
import Polysemy.Input (runInputConst)
import Polysemy.Embed (embedToFinal, runFinal)
import Wire.WebPushStore
import Wire.WebPushStore.Postgres (interpretWebPushStoreToPostgres)

-- | Run a WebPushStore effect stack inside the Gundeck monad.
runWebPush :: (MonadIO m) => Pool -> Sem '[WebPushStore, Input Pool, Error UsageError, Embed IO] a -> m (Either UsageError a)
runWebPush pool =
    liftIO
  . runFinal @IO
  . embedToFinal
  . runError @UsageError
  . runInputConst pool
  . interpretWebPushStoreToPostgres
```
Callers (`addWebSubscription`, `pushWeb`, `nativeTargets` web lookup in WP-HANDLERS / WP-DISPATCH / WP-FLOW) call effects via `runWebPush pool $ insertSubscription ...`, surfacing `UsageError` as the existing `mkError status500` server-error. This replaces the Cassandra `MonadClient` approach used by native push.

## Notes
- Gundeck now has TWO datastores: Cassandra (native push — unchanged) + Postgres (web push only). That's intentional and incremental.
- Migration ownership: the `webpush_subscriptions` migration lives in `wire-subsystems/postgres-migrations` (WP-DB); gundeck only *runs* `runAllMigrations`, which executes ALL embedded migrations. Confirm with infra whether gundeck points at a dedicated Postgres DB or a shared schema.
- Keep the pool sizing modest; web push dispatch is bounded by the push budget (see WP-DISPATCH).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `make c package=gundeck` compiles with new deps.
- [ ] Gundeck acquires a Hasql pool and runs migrations at startup.
- [ ] A trivial `runWebPush pool (pure ())` returns `Right ()` from the `Gundeck` monad.

## References
- `libs/wire-subsystems/src/Wire/Postgres.hs:94-155` (PGConstraints, runStatement)
- `libs/wire-subsystems/src/Wire/PostgresMigrations.hs:52` (runAllMigrations)
- `services/galley/src/Galley/App.hs:407-447` (storage-backend selection + runFinal pipeline, for reference)
- `services/gundeck/src/Gundeck/Env.hs:69-108` (createEnv — where pool is acquired)
- `services/gundeck/src/Gundeck/Options.hs:133` (Opts)
- Depends on: WP-DB (effect + interpreter + migration), WP-CFG (nothing — pool config lives here)
close_reason: Implemented: gundeck acquires a Hasql pool + runs Postgres migrations at startup (Options: _postgresql/_postgresqlPassword/_postgresqlPool via shared libpq convention; Env: initPostgresPool + runAllMigrations in createEnv, stored as _pgPool). Added Gundeck.Push.Web.Runner.runWebPush (minimal Sem runner using runM over WebPushStore/Input/Error/Embed). Unit test runWebPush pool (pure ()) == Right () passes; all 46 gundeck tests green; whole-repo cabal build all clean. Deploy YAMLs deferred to webpush rollout bead (consistent with galley/brig siblings).
